title: The time-invariant time-sharing conjecture for streaming codes
statement:
Let $d$ be the block-wise feedback delay. A **time-invariant scheme** is specified by a vector $\mathbf{x}=[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ of non-negative integers satisfying

$$
\sum_i x_i=d,
$$

and transmits $x_i$ linear combinations of the $i$ lowest-index unseen packets in each block. A time-sharing policy is a policy that alternates among such time-invariant schemes. **Time-invariant time-sharing conjecture.** For any coding scheme, there exists a corresponding time-sharing policy between time-invariant schemes that gives the same or strictly better $(\tau,\lambda)$ trade-off. This conjecture would reduce the analysis of general block-wise feedback schemes to time-sharing among the defined time-invariant schemes; whether every coding scheme admits such a policy is not established in the supplied text.
source_name: Gauri Joshi, Yuval Kochman and Gregory Wornell, “The Effect of Block-wise Feedback on the Throughput-Delay Trade-off in Streaming”, arXiv:1403.0259 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.0259

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2014).
